title: FancyZones does not notice when taskbar auto-hide is disabled

status.label: Refresh work areas after taskbar changes
status.detail: The current reporter confirms the stale-zone behavior on Windows 11 and PowerToys 0.101.2362; current FancyZones refreshes for SPI_SETWORKAREA notifications.

next_action.label: Reproduce the auto-hide transition on current Windows
next_action.reason: Confirm whether disabling auto-hide delivers the work-area notification FancyZones currently handles, then refresh cached work areas on the actual taskbar transition.

actions.label: Reproduce taskbar auto-hide transition
actions.note: The original report has a clear sequence; verify it on a current Windows 11 and PowerToys build before choosing which shell notification to handle.

reproduce.title: Verify FancyZones work-area refresh after disabling taskbar auto-hide
prerequisites: Taskbar auto-hide enabled and the taskbar at the bottom of the display
setup: Keep taskbar auto-hide enabled while starting or restarting FancyZones so it initializes with the taskbar hidden.
steps: Disable taskbar auto-hide without restarting Windows or FancyZones.
Shift-drag a window into a zone that reaches the bottom of the display.
Check whether the window's bottom edge remains above the visible taskbar.
reproduce.expected_result: FancyZones recomputes the work area after auto-hide is disabled, so the window is positioned above the visible taskbar.
reproduce.setup_prompt: On Windows 11, enable FancyZones and taskbar auto-hide, then restart FancyZones while the taskbar remains hidden.

judgment.rationale: The original report gives a specific state transition, and a Windows 11 commenter reconfirmed it on PowerToys 0.101.2362. Current FancyZones handles WM_SETTINGCHANGE only when wParam is SPI_SETWORKAREA, then invalidates cached work areas. If the auto-hide transition does not deliver that message, the cached bounds remain stale; a current reproduction should identify the exact shell notification before implementation.
evidence: The issue describes starting FancyZones while the taskbar is auto-hidden, disabling auto-hide without restarting, and then snapping a window into the old full-height zone.
A 2026-10-10 comment confirms the behavior on PowerToys 0.101.2362 and Windows 11 build 10.0.26200.9457.
Current upstream FancyZones.cpp handles WM_SETTINGCHANGE only when wParam equals SPI_SETWORKAREA and then calls OnDisplayChange(WorkArea), which updates cached work areas.
The issue's expected geometry is the current work area with the visible taskbar excluded.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce on a current Windows 11 build and observe the work-area notifications when auto-hide is disabled. Update FancyZones to invalidate cached work areas for the notification that actually accompanies this transition, then verify the snapped window remains above the taskbar.

fix_assessment.rationale: The report matches stale cached work-area geometry, and current code has a single explicit work-area invalidation gate for SPI_SETWORKAREA. The exact Windows notification accompanying the auto-hide transition should be confirmed before selecting the handler.

proposed_fixes.title: Invalidate FancyZones work areas on taskbar auto-hide changes
proposed_fixes.root_cause: FancyZones refreshes cached work areas for WM_SETTINGCHANGE only when wParam is SPI_SETWORKAREA. If Windows reports a taskbar auto-hide transition through a different shell notification, the cached work-area geometry can remain at the dimensions captured while the taskbar was hidden.
plan: Reproduce the issue on current Windows 11 and capture which setting or shell message is delivered when auto-hide is disabled.
In FancyZones::WndProc, route the confirmed taskbar/work-area transition to OnDisplayChange(DisplayChangeType::WorkArea) so UpdateWorkAreas recalculates the current monitor bounds.
Add or extend a test for changing taskbar auto-hide after FancyZones initialization, and retain the existing display-change and work-area-change behavior.
verification: With auto-hide enabled at FancyZones startup, disabling it without restarting refreshes the bottom zone to exclude the taskbar.
Re-enabling auto-hide refreshes the zone to the monitor edge.
Existing display-resolution, taskbar-position, and virtual-desktop work-area behavior remains unchanged.

confidence.rationale: The stale-geometry symptom is confirmed on a recent Windows 11 build and current code has an explicit work-area refresh gate, but the exact message emitted by the auto-hide transition needs a current reproduction.

issue_context.summary: FancyZones can retain a work area that extends behind the taskbar after taskbar auto-hide is disabled.
known_information: The original report gives steps that start FancyZones while the taskbar is hidden, disable auto-hide, and then snap a window into a bottom zone.
A 2026-10-10 commenter reports the issue on PowerToys 0.101.2362 and Windows 11 build 10.0.26200.9457.
Current upstream FancyZones::WndProc refreshes work areas for WM_SETTINGCHANGE when wParam is SPI_SETWORKAREA and for WM_DISPLAYCHANGE.
inferences: The taskbar auto-hide transition may not reach FancyZones through the SPI_SETWORKAREA branch, leaving previously cached geometry in use.
Routing the actual transition notification through the existing WorkArea refresh path should update zone bounds without changing normal zone layout behavior.
issue_context.analysis: The issue's sequence isolates a stale work-area cache: FancyZones is initialized while the taskbar is hidden, and the mismatch appears only after auto-hide is disabled. Current code already has a cache invalidation route for work-area changes, but only for SPI_SETWORKAREA. Confirm the notification delivered by the current Windows build before adding another message or shell hook.
initial_investigation: Read the full issue and all four comments; the latest commenter supplied a current Windows 11 and PowerToys version.
Inspected current upstream FancyZones.cpp: WM_SETTINGCHANGE checks SPI_SETWORKAREA and calls OnDisplayChange(WorkArea); that path invokes UpdateWorkAreas.
